findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted condition and wrong substring indices
findings.body: The token id has the form `ssttgg:uuid`, so the grant shortcut is at chars 4..6, i.e. `substring(4, 6)`. The matcher uses `substring(3, 5)`, which covers the 2nd char of the token type and the 1st char of the grant. It also returns false when the substring EQUALS the expected shortcut, so the condition is inverted. Because indices 3..5 never equal a 2-char shortcut such as `ac`, the check never fires and the grant shortcut is never verified. Every test that uses `expectCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh` and similar helpers passes without validating the grant type, and the wrong code would fail if the check ever matched. It should be `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

findings.title: Null check for rawTokenId actually checks grantType
findings.body: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` repeats the grantType check, so `rawTokenId` is never validated. A null raw id is accepted and later encoded into the string `"xxxxxx:null"`. It should be `requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`.

findings.title: New abstract method on SPI interface breaks existing custom grant factories
findings.body: `getShortcut()` is added as an abstract method on the public `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` SPI. Any third-party grant type factory will no longer compile or load. `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` also calls it and puts the result into maps, so a null or duplicate shortcut from a custom grant would fail startup or corrupt the mapping. Consider a default implementation, or tolerate missing shortcuts and map them to the unknown value.

findings.title: Token type and session type derived from ambient/early state, not the actual token
findings.body: The lightweight flag comes from `getShouldUseLightweightToken(session)`, which reads `session.getContext().getClient()` rather than the `client` that `initToken` is creating the token for. In flows where the context client differs from the token's client (for example token exchange), the encoded token type can be wrong. The session type is read from the user session at the moment the access token is created. For offline-scope flows the access token is generated before the offline session is created (when the refresh token is generated), so it is encoded as `on` even though the request ends up using an offline session. This defeats the stated purpose of using the type to pick the right session lookup.

findings.title: Parsing throws for any token id containing ':' that is not in the 6-char format
findings.body: `getTokenContextFromTokenId` returns an UNKNOWN context only when there is no ':'. If the id contains ':' but the prefix is not exactly 6 chars with known shortcuts (for example tokens issued by older or custom code, or ids with other prefixes), it throws IllegalArgumentException. Callers that later use this to inspect arbitrary tokens will fail with a 500 instead of falling back to UNKNOWN. Legacy or foreign ids should degrade gracefully.

findings.title: Context grantType is captured once and the copy constructor was removed
findings.body: `grantType` is read from `formParams` in the constructor only. `setFormParams` can later replace the form params, which leaves `grantType` stale. The public copy constructor `Context(Context)` was also removed from this SPI class, which breaks any external code that used it.

findings.title: Unused import added
findings.body: `TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory` is imported but never used in this file.
